title: Annotate model manifests with runtime constraints and publish canonical performance baselines
creator: Asha Patel
description: When new models are onboarded we currently publish minimal manifest entries and a pinned version. This ticket expands the onboarding manifest schema to include explicit runtime constraints (max_seq_length, preferred_kernels, memory_working_set), a recommended pinning policy for experimental vs stable builds, and attached canonical performance baselines (latency p50/p95, throughput at common batch sizes, and cost-per-1k-tokens estimates). The goal is to make runtime decisioning (routing, fallback, autoscaling) deterministic and to reduce surprises for Dedicated/Private customers when they pin variants. This work touches the manifest linter, the catalog publish pipeline, and docs that teach engineers how to choose pins and read performance profiles.
acceptance_criteria: Manifest schema adds runtime_constraints, benchmarks, and pin_policy fields and is backwards-compatible
A catalog linter job validates new fields and fails builds for malformed constraints
Perf publishing pipeline consumes the benchmark artifact and attaches a signed baseline to the model entry
Docs updated with an example manifest, interpretation guide, and pinning best-practices
QA verifies canonical baselines for 3 recent models across two instance types and compares to historical perf within 15%
steps: Define schema additions and field semantics in model_manifest.md draft
Implement schema in onboarding pipeline and update ingestion code to persist new fields
Add manifest linter rules and unit tests
Wire benchmark runner to publish signed baseline JSON to catalog and store fingerprint
Update catalog UI and API to surface the new fields
Write docs + examples and publish to docs.redwood.ai; include rollback guidance
Run QA benchmarks on models: openai-like-7b, llama3-13b, falcon-instruct-7b (example set)
Ship schema changes behind a feature flag for 2-week canary before forcing linter enforcement
